grh_c408a48f194fce96e1d1.title: Woman Who Runs Dress Store
paragraphs: Harriet Niles runs a successful dress shop in Rivers End and is raising her young daughter Toby in peace, but Harriet is living under an assumed name. She is actually Doris Fleming, widow of a notorious man who murdered one of her former admirers, was convicted and later died in prison. Dr. Christian helped Doris make a new start so Toby could grow up without carrying her fathers scandal. A self-righteous local man named John discovers the secret and insists that Harriet surrender her daughter, arguing that a child should not be raised by a woman with such a past. He pressures and effectively blackmails her until Harriet prepares to leave town and even considers giving Toby up. Dr. Christian investigates John in return and confronts him with what appears to be an official California report showing that he too served time in prison. Terrified of exposure, John confesses that he did spend five years in San Quentin and admits that bitterness over the woman involved in his own case has driven his crusade against Harriet. The report is actually from the state agriculture department; Dr. Christian needed only Johns confession. Rather than expose him, the doctor offers to help cure his resentment, while Harriet and Toby are allowed to keep their home and life in Rivers End.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on December 26, 1937. It is listed as episode 8 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt. Other credited names include Art Gilmore as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_c429f52f1e9352ff26cd.title: Suzie's Cue
paragraphs: In Vienna, Harry teams with the broke Countess Suzie and her associate Carl to steal a wealthy baron's valuable necklace. Suzie supplies the safe key, Carl distracts the baron at the front door, and Harry enters by the balcony and takes the jewels. Suzie then convinces Harry that Carl plans to double-cross them, so Harry confronts Carl at gunpoint and takes possession of the necklace. Police arrive moments later, arrest Carl and recover the jewels. The inspector reveals that Carl really is a respected aristocratic former officer and not the treacherous impostor Suzie described. Suzie admits she invented the story and tipped off police so Carl would be removed, leaving Harry free for her instead of receiving a share of the robbery.

grh_c42ae8d22a7a839800b2.title: The Evil That Men Do
paragraphs: Scientist Alexander Kiran develops Benefactral, a drug that suppresses criminal impulses for forty-eight hours, and proposes putting it into the city water supply. The apparent cure for crime immediately threatens politicians, police, security businesses and others whose livelihoods depend on the existing system, and Kiran is pressured to abandon it. He plans a secret reservoir treatment with an ally whose own dose has worn off, only to discover that the human impulses he hoped to eliminate return as soon as the drug does. The experiment ends as a dark satire on both engineered virtue and the interests built around crime.
